207513684_4c3597a6.text: Direct input from entorhinal cortex produces a 5- to 6-fold larger EPSP at the soma of CA2 compared with CA1 pyramidal neurons, which is sufficient to drive action potential output from CA2 but not CA1 (Srinivas et al., 2017). This difference results from more efficient dendritic propagation in CA2 than CA1 due to differences in dendritic morphology and dendritic expression of the hyperpolarization-activated cation current (Ih) (Srinivas et al., 2017).
